stories.intro: *humming something at dawn, alone, while the rest of {village} is still asleep* Oh! {player}. You caught me. *smooths their veils* I wasn't born here, you know. I came from a village far in the west, nine days on Vell's back. Some mornings I miss it so much my veils go limp. I'd like a taste of home, if a walker could find one.

requests.title: A taste of the west
requests.prompt: At home our islands grew melons right in the clouds. Here it's peaches, peaches, peaches, and I love them, truly. But bring me eight slices of melon? I want to taste the west.
requests.thanks: *bites into one and shuts their eyes* Oh, that's it. Pink and cold, and the juice runs down your wrist. *wipes it on a veil-tip, unashamed* Don't tell the gardeners about the face I just made.

requests.title: Western breakfast
requests.prompt: At home we drizzled honey on the melon, first thing in the morning. Walker bees put their honey in bottles, I'm told, which is very tidy of them. Two bottles, please?
requests.thanks: *drizzles it over a slice and eats it in two bites, licking a thumb* Now that's breakfast. That's a western breakfast. I'll be humming all day.

requests.title: Petals for the hair
requests.prompt: In the west, everyone wore petals in their hair on high days. Pink ones. I've no idea where you'd find such things down there, but walkers find everything. Eight handfuls?
requests.thanks: *tucks a handful into their hair, then another, until they're more petal than Cirri* Well? Do I look like I'm from somewhere? *turns slowly* I feel like I'm from somewhere.

stories.waiting: *humming at dawn, a little louder each day* Hm? Oh, nothing. A tune from home. There's more to the west than melons, {player}, and I'm not sure I'm ready to say it. Come and talk a few more days.
stories.ready: *finishes the tune and lets it hang in the air* You've heard me singing at dawn. You're the only one awake enough to notice. Stay a light breeze, and I'll tell you what it is.
stories.confide: At home we sing the Evensong, like everyone. But we also sing the dawn up: the whole village, every morning, before Aure is even awake. Here nobody does. I've sung it alone for fourteen years. *quieter* Last month a whale-rider brought word. My parents are getting old, and they asked if I'll come home for a season. I'm afraid if I go, I won't want to come back. And if I stay, I'll sing alone for ever.

endings.label: Teach the dawn-song here
endings.text: *the petals tremble* Teach it here. Of course. Start with the children; they're up early anyway, and they'll sing anything. A little dawn-song for {village}, and I won't be singing alone. *suddenly shy* I'll send word home, so my parents know it's sung here too. Here. A chime from the west. It's tuned to dawn.
endings.memory: You told {name} to teach the dawn-song in {village}, starting with the children.

endings.label: Fly home for a season
endings.text: *a long breath* Go home. For a season. Sing the dawn up with the ones who taught me, and sit with my parents while there's time. And if I don't want to come back... *a small laugh* I'll come anyway, because I'll miss these peaches. Here. A chime from the west. Hang it, and fair wind till I'm home.
endings.memory: You told {name} to fly home west for a season, while their parents are still there.

stories.title: The Cushion Never Given
stories.intro: *hovering with something soft and old in their lap: a cushion, rose at the edges, flattened with years* This? It's nothing. *it is clearly not nothing* In {village}, when you ask someone to share your nest, you weave them a cushion first. I wove this one when I was young. It's gone flat as a still day. I'd like to make it soft again.

requests.title: Something soft
requests.prompt: The cloud I filled it with has gone tired. Walker birds shed the softest things; I've felt them at the market. Sixteen feathers, and I'll fill it up the way it was.
requests.thanks: *works the feathers in, one by one, and the cushion slowly rises* There. As soft as the day I finished it. *pats it, and then doesn't let go* Thank you, {player}. It looks ready. As if that matters.

requests.title: A sweet scent
requests.prompt: A nest-cushion should smell sweet. I tucked peach blossom in the seams once, but that's long gone. Walker lilac, the tall purple flower, smells of evening, they say. Two, please?
requests.thanks: *breathes it in and laughs softly* It does smell of evening. Of Vell, almost, when the song carries. *tucks a sprig into each seam* There. Sweet again.

requests.title: Rose for the edges
requests.prompt: The rose edge has faded to grey. I'd like the colour back. Walkers make dyes out of flowers, I'm told. Two of pink?
requests.thanks: *paints the faded edge with a fingertip, slowly, all the way round* There's the rose. Exactly as it was. *holds it out at arm's length* It's a good cushion. I was a good weaver, even then.

stories.waiting: *the cushion sits plump on their nest, and they straighten it whenever they pass* No, I'm not giving it to anyone. Don't look at me like that. There's a story in it, but it's an old, soft one. Come back a few more days.
stories.ready: *holds the cushion up so the rose edge catches the light* You've been very good not to ask who it was for. Anyone else would have. I suppose that's why I'll tell you.
stories.confide: Someone in {village}. I won't say who; don't guess. We were young, and I spent a whole winter weaving this, and on the morning I meant to give it, I saw them laughing with someone else over the koi pool, and I knew. They've shared a nest with that someone ever since, three islets over, happily. I've kept this forty years and never said a word. I'm glad they're happy. Truly. I only wish I'd said it.

endings.label: Give it to someone brave
endings.text: *nods* There's a young one by the Loom House who looks at someone the way I used to. Trembles every time they pass. I'll give them this and say: weave your own, but take this for courage, and say it. Out loud. *a soft laugh* Let it do its job at last. Here. A little veilcloth. Every nest needs some.
endings.memory: You told {name} to give the old cushion to a shy young Cirri, for the courage to speak.

endings.label: Weave it into your veil
endings.text: *picks a thread loose from the seam, then another* I'll unpick it, and the weavers can weave the cloud into the tips of my veils. Then it flies with me. It was never wasted, {player}. I loved someone well and quietly, and they're happy. That's not nothing. Here. A little veilcloth. Every nest needs some.
endings.memory: You told {name} to weave the old cushion's cloud into their veils, so it flies with them.

stories.title: The Last Bell of Orrowmere
stories.intro: *hovering at the rim, looking a long way off* We Cirri keep our faces, walker. We wear our years in our veils, and mine are thin as breath. Do you know the Ruined Belltowers? Broken islands, bells fallen in. One was my first home. Orrowmere. I'm the last who heard its bell. I'd like to hear one like it again before I go up past the blue.

requests.title: A bell from below
requests.prompt: Orrowmere's bell was iron, from the bell-villages below, like yours. We had no business with iron in the sky. But I'd like to hear that sound once more. Bring me a walker bell, {player}?
requests.thanks: *rings it once, very gently, and the note rolls out over the clouds; their eyes stay shut until it's gone* Yes. That's it. Heavier than ours. Sadder. Exactly right. Thank you, walker.

requests.title: Mending for a long flight
requests.prompt: My veils are thin as breath. The weavers say they'll mend them for one more long flight, if I bring night-moth membrane. Nasty things, night-moths. Two pieces? Walkers are braver at night than we are.
requests.thanks: *smooths the membrane flat, feeling its weight* That will hold. For a while longer, anyway. Long enough. *a crooked smile* Don't look so sad. I said long enough, not too long.

requests.title: Flowers for the ruin
requests.prompt: Little white bells that grow on the ground, I'm told. Lily of the valley. Orrowmere was all bells; it seems right. Three, please. One for each of my parents, and one for the island.
requests.thanks: *holds them up and shakes one gently, listening* No sound. Silent bells. *a soft laugh* That's the right kind for where they're going. Thank you.

stories.waiting: *rings the bell softly at odd hours and listens to the note go* The young ones think I've gone strange. Let them. There's a reason it matters, and it's the last long story I have. Come back a few more days, {player}.
stories.ready: *rests one thin hand on the bell* I've told the Orrowmere story a hundred times: the village that grew too heavy. I've never told my part. You've been patient. Come close; my voice isn't what it was.
stories.confide: My parent was Orrowmere's bellkeeper. When the island began to sink, a little lower every year, the elders said: take the bell down, it's too heavy. My parent wouldn't. The bell was the village's voice, they said. The night the island slipped into the clouds, we all flew. My parent stayed in the tower, ringing. I was nine summers old. I heard it ring all the way down.

endings.label: Ring it at the ruin
endings.text: *sets a thin hand on the bell* Then we'll go to Orrowmere one last time, you with the bell, me with the lilies. We'll hang it on what's left of the tower and I'll ring it once, for a bellkeeper who couldn't let go. And we'll leave it there for the next one who finds the ruin. Here. A crystal from Orrowmere's tower. It still rings when the wind touches it.
endings.memory: You told {name} to hang the bell at the ruin of Orrowmere and ring it once for their parent.

endings.label: Ring it at the Evensong
endings.text: *looks toward the Veil Court* No more flights to sunken places. I'll ring it here, once, at the Evensong, and tell the young ones what it is: the voice of a village that held on too tight. Then you'll carry it back down to the ground, where it can't sink anything. Here. A crystal from Orrowmere's tower. It still rings when the wind touches it.
endings.memory: You told {name} to ring the bell once at the Evensong and tell the young ones about Orrowmere.
